Arrive at Bogotá’s international airport, where you’ll be met and transferred to **Hotel Novotel Bogota Parque 93**.

After you check in, you’ll start exploring the capital. The Spanish founded Bogotá in the 16th century on the site of earlier Indigenous settlements. The city’s name is associated with that of a Chibcha chief. Today, Bogotá is a large metropolis with historic districts, museums, restaurants, cafés and modern development.

The first part of the tour takes you through La Candelaria, Bogotá’s best-known historic district. Colonial buildings, churches and small squares survive here, along with streets lined by old façades.

A main stop is the Gold Museum, with its extensive collection of pre-Hispanic gold artefacts. In addition to the gold pieces, the museum displays more than 20,000 objects from the pre-Columbian period.

Next, visit the Casa de la Moneda and the Botero Museum. The mint was founded in the 17th century and occupies a colonial mansion. Nearby is the museum named for Fernando Botero, who donated a large collection of his own work to the city. The museum also displays works by Dalí and other European artists.

After the museums, stroll through Plaza de Bolívar. The square is home to a monument to the first president, the cathedral and other landmarks in the historic centre. If you pass the presidential palace around 17:00, you may see the changing of the guard.

The tour ends with a ride up Monserrate. The mountain was named for the cathedral of the Black Madonna, built in the 17th century, and rises about 500 metres above the city. A funicular takes you to the summit, with views over Bogotá and the surrounding Andean plateau.

**Included in the tour:** admission to the Gold Museum, Casa de la Moneda and the Botero Museum, guide services and a private transfer.

**Note:** The Gold Museum is closed on Mondays. Casa de la Moneda and the Botero Museum are closed on Tuesdays.
